subject: Clarify invoice line-item mapping + volume rebate mechanics
messages:
From: Ari Kaplan <ari@quantara.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood pricing / invoice export question

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the latency numbers. Procurement asked me to confirm one thing before we move to SOW: on our existing contracts with other vendors we can see per-token slabs broken out on the export (counts at each price band) so we can reconcile committed discounts against line items. Can Redwood provide a CSV export that shows token bands + per-token effective rate for each billing period?

Also: we negotiated a volume rebate in the LOI that is applied retroactively based on quarterly usage tiers (e.g., Tier A 0-200M, Tier B 200M-1B). How does that appear on the invoice — as a credit line, or do you show an adjusted per-token unit price? Procurement would like a consistent mapping so internal finance can automate reconciliation.

I’m attaching the draft SOW and a sample usage file from our current provider for reference.

Thanks,
Ari Kaplan
Head of Platform Partnerships
Quantara Labs

Attachments: Quantara_SOW.pdf (application/pdf), Usage_Sample_CSV.csv (text/csv)
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Ari Kaplan <ari@quantara.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood pricing / invoice export question

Hi Ari — great to hear the demo landed well. Short answers up front: yes, we can surface a per-token slab breakdown in the usage export, and we represent volume rebates as discrete invoice credit lines by default (with a net line that indicates the final effective cost). That said, finance integrations prefer different flavors (some want adjusted unit price rows instead).

Couple quick clarifying questions so I loop the right folks:
- Do you need the slab counts broken out per model (e.g., gptx-16k) or just aggregated across your account?
- Is Quantara’s ledger automation sensitive to line-item IDs or just the description/amount?

I’m looping in Rishi (pricing/finance) and Jordan (billing ops) to propose an export schema and confirm how the rebate credit would be surfaced. We can provide a one-off mapping for the first two invoices to ensure your AR script matches.

Next steps: Rishi/Jordan — can you review the attached sample usage and propose a CSV template that includes: account_id, invoice_period, model, token_band_low, token_band_high, token_count, unit_price, line_item_id? Also need to confirm whether to emit an explicit rebate credit row vs. adjusted unit price.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: procurement@quantara.com <procurement@quantara.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: Ari Kaplan <ari@quantara.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 08:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood pricing / invoice export question

Olga,

Thanks for the quick reply. For onboarding we prefer slab counts per model — that makes our chargeback more accurate across product teams. Our finance system matches on a combination of invoice line_item_code and description. If you can include a stable line_item_code (e.g., RID-TOKEN-<band>-<model>) that would be ideal.

Regarding rebates: procurement prefers to see the rebate as a separate credit line (negative amount) so we can apply it through our accounting workflow; adjusted unit price rows make it hard for audit trails.

If you can prepare a sample CSV for December (using the attached sample usage) that follows the template below, we can validate it internally:
- columns: account_id, invoice_period_start, invoice_period_end, model, token_band_low, token_band_high, token_count, unit_price, gross_amount, rebate_credit_amount, net_amount, line_item_code

We expect the SOW to go to legal this week; this mapping will speed PO issuance.

Procurement
Quantara Labs
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: Ari Kaplan <ari@quantara.com>, procurement@quantara.com
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Redwood pricing / invoice export question — internal next steps

Team — forwarding procurement’s preferences. Quick asks before I respond:
1) Rishi — can you confirm whether Finance is comfortable outputting a separate rebate credit row on host invoices for Dedicated/Hosted customers? Do we need a new GL code?
2) Jordan — can Billing Ops emit the CSV with a stable line_item_code per band+model and include both gross_amount and rebate_credit_amount columns? If we can do a one-month pilot CSV for the sample usage Ari attached, that will unblock PO.
3) Marissa — want you on the reply to Procurement to keep the track stable and ensure legal sees the exact wording for the SOW.

I’ve drafted a sample mapping below (feel free to edit before we send):

- RID-TOKEN-0-200M-gptx-16k — token band 0-200M, unit_price $0.0002, gross_amount = token_count * unit_price
- RID-TOKEN-200M-1B-gptx-16k — token band 200M-1B, unit_price $0.00015
- Rebate line: RID-REBATE-Q4-2026-Quantara — negative credit applied at invoice level with reference to deal_id QTL-2026-0921

If we can turn around a CSV example by EOD Thursday (17th) I’ll attach it to our SOW response.

Thanks,
Olga
